_source: City of St. Petersburg Comprehensive Plan — Future Land Use Element. Verify current adopted densities/intensities at stpete.org/compplan

CBD.name: Central Business District
CBD.description: Downtown St. Petersburg core; highest-intensity urban mixed use
CBD.notes: No residential density cap in CBD — governed by FAR and design standards. FAR up to 10.0 base; bonuses available. Full range of downtown uses permitted.

RMU.name: Regional Mixed Use
RMU.description: High-intensity mixed-use nodes serving regional market; corridors and activity centers outside downtown
RMU.notes: Intended for regional commercial nodes, transit corridors, and urban centers outside downtown. Mixed residential and commercial at high intensity.

CMU.name: Community Mixed Use
CMU.description: Community-scale commercial corridors and mixed-use activity centers
CMU.notes: Mid-intensity mixed use. Ground-floor active uses encouraged. Serves community commercial needs along primary corridors.

RFH.name: Residential Future High
RFH.notes: High-density residential areas. Typically located near transit and urban corridors. Confirm currently adopted density cap with City Comprehensive Plan.

RFM.name: Residential Future Medium
RFM.description: Medium-density residential — duplexes, triplexes, small apartment buildings
RFM.notes: Moderate residential density. Intended for small multi-family and attached single-family housing types in established neighborhoods.

RFL.name: Residential Future Low
RFL.notes: Preserves traditional single-family neighborhoods. Typical for established low-density residential areas of St. Pete.

RFR.name: Residential Future Rural
RFR.description: Very low-density rural and estate residential
RFR.notes: Low-intensity rural residential on large lots. Limited to areas with rural character, typically with acreage.

EMP.name: Employment
EMP.description: Employment-generating uses: office, light industrial, business park, R&D
EMP.notes: Non-residential employment land. Residential uses generally not permitted. Focuses on job creation and business activity.

IND.name: Industrial
IND.description: Heavy and general industrial uses; warehousing, manufacturing, distribution
IND.notes: Industrial land uses. Residential uses not permitted. Buffering from residential required. Confirm current adopted standards with City planning.

PQP.name: Public / Quasi-Public
PQP.description: Government, civic, institutional, educational, and utility facilities
PQP.notes: Public and institutional lands. FAR and use subject to specific use approval. Includes schools, hospitals, government offices, utilities.

PSP.name: Parks, Shores and Preserve
PSP.description: Parks, open space, waterfront shoreline, and conservation areas
PSP.notes: No residential development. Minimal impervious surface. Preservation of natural, parks, and waterfront resources.
